title: Trump Rules Out US-China Joint Ventures on AI
key_facts: Trump said at the launch of America.gov, an AI-powered government services website, that he will not enter a joint venture with China on AI.
He argued it would hand over secrets to America's main economic rival and said the US is 'leading by a lot'.
MediaNama says the BBC reported the remarks on Tuesday 29 Sep 2026.
Trump and Xi Jinping agreed to set up an AI incident notification hotline and continue talks on AI risks; the rejection covers joint development and shared governance only.
The same day Trump announced a voluntary, two-page accord signed by leaders of six US tech companies, which he called 'morally binding' although it has no legal force.
He also signed an order telling agencies to say 'superintelligence' instead of 'AI' in official communications.
quote_evidence: Trump's rejection applies only to joint development and shared governance, not to all forms of contact.
The two leaders agreed to establish an AI incident notification hotline and continue discussions on AI risks.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows the White House line on AI with China: compete, keep a risk hotline, no joint work.
notes: MediaNama opens with 'We missed this earlier' and relays a BBC report; event is a week old, so score lowered.
